correctness.rationale: The derived center forces a unique block form. Preservation of Lie brackets gives the conformal symplectic identity; idempotence gives the three block-idempotence relations. For the center-preserving branch, nondegeneracy and idempotence force the identity. For the center-annihilating branch, im A is totally isotropic and c factors through it. Fixed images correspond bijectively to \(\(q^{r(2n-r)}\)\) complementary kernels, proving the formula for every n and prime power q. Exact exhaustive matrix checks include full unrestricted dimension-three Lie maps and GF(4), plus independent finite symplectic-space checks; general validity follows from symbolic proof, not sample enumeration.

value.rationale: A Lie-algebra retract is a split subobject, whose occurrence and number of sections are not determined by an ordinary subalgebra census. The theorem gives a complete natural rank invariant for an infinite family, a central-obstruction rank gap \(n+1,\ldots,2n\), and exact \(\(q^{r(2n-r)}\)\) counts onto each individual allowable image. This pinpoints structural splitness and local multiplicities; not merely known isotropic subspace enumeration or arbitrary finite-case data.
